title: Ramayan

fact_notes: This is an epic, not history: every story line follows the Valmiki Ramayana's account (Bala, Ayodhya, Aranya, Kishkindha, Sundara, Yuddha kandas). Script narrates what the epic tells, in the present/past of the story.
Ravana, ten-headed king of Lanka (Dashanana) - Valmiki, Aranya and Yuddha Kanda.

Setu: the vanara army builds a bridge to Lanka; floating stones are the popular telling (Nala's construction in Yuddha Kanda; 'stones that float' is later tradition, widely cited). Keep 'floating stones' as tradition, or change to 'a bridge of stone' for strictness.
Rama lifts and breaks Shiva's bow at Janaka's court to win Sita - Bala Kanda.
Kaikeyi claims two boons from Dasharatha: Bharata crowned, Rama exiled 14 years - Ayodhya Kanda.
Golden deer is the demon Maricha in disguise - Aranya Kanda.
Ravana appears as a mendicant (sannyasi) and carries Sita off in the Pushpaka chariot through the sky; Jatayu fights and is mortally wounded - Aranya Kanda.
Sugriva, vanara king; Hanuman his minister - Kishkindha Kanda.
Hanuman leaps to Lanka, finds Sita in the Ashoka grove, sets Lanka on fire with his burning tail - Sundara Kanda.
Rama kills Ravana with the Brahmastra arrow - Yuddha Kanda.
Diwali is widely associated with Rama's return to Ayodhya, especially in north India (other regions tie it to other stories). 'Millions' is conservative.
Valmiki Ramayana: about 24,000 shlokas, traditionally counted; seven kandas.
Dating: scholars place the composition roughly between the 7th-5th century BCE and the 3rd century CE; 'more than two thousand years' is commonly cited.
